010aa00becaf980e: Unknown crims compromised LiteLLM's release process on Wednesday, distributing a malicious version (1.107.0) containing malware designed to steal cloud and AI credentials and a remote access trojan (RAT) capable of executing arbitrary code on infected machines through PyPI and Docker registries.

PyPI quarantined the trojanized version of the popular open source AI gateway within hours, and the Docker image (litellm/litellm:1.107.0) was removed from both Docker Hub and GHCR soon after - but anyone who ran the compromised package on any platform should assume their secrets have been stolen.

“Check for /tmp/.pc_once_* (the exfil has already fired if this file exists) and /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock (the C2 daemon ran or is still running if this file exists),” advised Aikido Security malware hunter Ilyas Makari. “The same applies to anyone who ran the official Docker image litellm/litellm:1.107.0, or pulled it via the latest, main-latest, or main-stable tags.”
The most recent safe version is v1.106.2.

While it’s too early to tell the scale of this latest LiteLLM supply chain attack – an earlier LiteLLM compromise in March potentially exposed more than 2,500 organizations and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines worldwide, according to CloudSEK – make sure to take these measures seriously, and check environments for any indicators of compromise.

Aikido, Google’s Wiz cloud security biz, and supply-chain security provider Socket have all published extensive threat-hunting and mitigation instructions for LiteLLM users and security teams, so give those a read stat.

LiteLLM, developed by BerriAI, provides a common interface for LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini, and receives about 23 million weekly downloads. This means a compromised installation can run alongside LLM provider API keys, cloud identities, and database connection strings - and expose a ton of valuable credentials, secrets, and other sensitive data to whoever uploaded the malicious package.
“Teams using 1.107.0 should stop deploying it and investigate environments where Python ran after installation, including proxy containers and CI runners,” Socket researchers said on Wednesday.

The malicious version was uploaded at 11:39 UTC, and according to Wiz kids Benjamin Read and Rami McCarthy, the payload originates with malicious commits made on github.com/Berri-AI/litellm, which is a hyphenated variant of the legitimate BerriAI organization.

Miscreants used this repo to inject the three malicious files into the LiteLLM release pipeline. These, according to Makari, include cook.pth, which causes the second file, cook.py, to run automatically every time Python is invoked on the machine, without any additional user action.

Meanwhile, cook.py contains the infostealer, and the third file, sitecustomize.py, is the RAT. Python also executes the RAT at interpreter startup, and this file spawns a background daemon that polls the attacker's infrastructure every hour for new commands to execute.
Upon executing, the infostealer harvests a ton of sensitive data across 16 modules targeting browsers, cloud providers, and AI services, according to Read and McCarthy.

It steals browser credentials and cookies from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari, along with AWS credentials from ~/.aws/, environment variables, and EC2/ECS instance metadata (IMDS). It also collects users’ Google Cloud Platform service account keys and application default credentials, along with Microsoft Azure tokens from the CLI cache.
And then it also swipes API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and other LLM providers, plus SSH private keys, GPG keys, and shell history files.

The malware then encrypts all of this stolen data using AES-256-CBC, wraps the encryption key with an RSA-4096 public key, and sends the encrypted data via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled domain: http://www[.]litellm[.]dev/healthcheck.
BerriAI did not respond to The Register’s inquiries. This is an emerging story, and we will continue to update it as we learn more details.®

ec389b6ace81a23d: More than half of CIOs are likely to miss their AI-related ROI targets next year, according to Forrester.
The analyst firm's State Of AI Survey 2026 found that 45 percent of AI decision-makers need positive ROI within a year to consider their investments successful.
Some tech leaders will get better at tying AI spend to planned returns. However, Forrester expects success to be confined to isolated use cases rather than whole programs, which won't be enough.
“As with prior emerging technologies, organizational structures, processes, and ways of working need to change to drive measurable, firmwide results with AI,” the report says.
Only 22 percent of AI decision-makers report a positive AI impact on EBITDA (earnings before income tax, depreciation and amortization) over the past 12 months.
“This mismatch between the investment into technology adoption and organizational change will delay the realization of heightened ROI targets,” the report adds.
The money will keep flowing through IT budgets regardless. In its Technology & Security Predictions, Forrester claimed AI will account for 20 percent of all business technology spend next year.

Sharyn Leaver, chief research officer at Forrester, said that will increase the pressure on leaders to prove AI's value while keeping costs, infrastructure, and risk under control. “At the same time, emerging technologies, geopolitical pressures, and the growing use of AI across technology operations will introduce new complexities and potential points of failure,” she said.

While tech teams struggle to get returns from growing AI spending, they will try to get more bang for their buck by investing in open-weight GenAI models, which can approach similar performance to the leading proprietary systems, at a fraction of the cost. Open-weight models will represent half of AI tokens but only five percent of enterprise spend, Forrester predicts.

“Open-weight models such as Gemma, Llama, or Qwen are good enough for the enterprise workloads that generate the most token volume, such as document processing, customer support conversations, internal knowledge search, and the routine substeps inside agentic workflows,” Forrester said.

Frontier models, including Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, and Google's Gemini 4 Argon, will be reserved for “the few deep knowledge and critical task automations where errors are expensive, but the token count will tip toward open weight”, Forrester said.

7ae486925b0f5ddc: Make sure you don’t say anything mean or secret after hanging up a call on Signal, as a bug in the encrypted messaging app’s calling library could prevent a call from ending properly, potentially leaving audio and possibly video active.

The vulnerability, CVE-2026-113380, was published by MITRE on Tuesday and given a CVSS score of 9.3, marking it as a critical issue in Signal’s open-source RingRTC library in every single version before 2.72.0. That update was pushed out last month, but the vulnerability wasn’t made public until now.

RingRTC is Signal’s own calling library built on top of WebRTC, a technology introduced in 2011 that has since become widely used for voice and video communication over the internet. RingRTC provides Signal-specific calling functionality using WebRTC, which already encrypts media traffic, but that isn't stopping RingRTC from failing to hang up calls in certain conditions, according to the CVE report.

What’s happening is, in essence, a denial-of-service attack on RingRTC’s finite state machine (FSM) event queue, which handles events involved in managing calls. If one of the people on the call saturates the FSM queue with requests, it can become overwhelmed and fail to process a hangup request, preventing the call from terminating properly. The vulnerability is classified as CWE-754, or improper checking for unusual or exceptional conditions, according to a report posted to GitHub.
A conceptual proof of concept is available in the GitHub report linked above, using a Python script to simulate how flooding an event queue can prevent a hangup request from being processed.
Were a malicious actor to exploit this, the person on the other end may think the call has been terminated, but either or both of their video and audio channels could still be open.

The attack complexity is considered low according to the CVE, and while CISA’s known exploited vulnerabilities catalog doesn’t indicate this has been spotted in the wild, Signal users ought to ensure they’ve updated their apps - mobile and desktop - to the latest versions to ensure they don’t end up being caught on a hot mic without any notice.

Comparing RingRTC 2.72.0 to the previous version indicates that Signal's fix allows the call's finite state machine (FSM) to detect termination requests independently of the event queue, while adding a timeout to prevent stalled processing from indefinitely blocking a hangup.

It's not entirely clear from Signal's release notes when the fixed version of RingRTC reached the Android, iOS, and desktop versions of its apps. Signal Desktop's release history indicates that RingRTC 2.72.0 was incorporated in September, but the precise rollout dates across all platforms remain unclear. We’ve reached out to Signal to learn more, but haven’t heard back.
In the meantime, best to update your installation to be sure you’re not still vulnerable. That, and watch what you say after hanging up a call. ®

61ce8fd1c476c25f: RAMALLAH: Israeli forces on Wednesday briefly detained a US congressional candidate as he joined activists supporting Palestinians harvesting olives in the face of threats by extremist settlers.

Brad Lander, a left-wing Democrat who is expected to easily win a House seat in New York City on Nov 3, posted on social media that he was detained along with a group of rabbis and volunteers as they harvested olives west of Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank.
"The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn't a crime under any law I know," Lander wrote on X.
He later wrote that he was released on account of his prominence, adding that "Palestinians face far worse consequences every day."
The Israeli foreign ministry lashed out at Lander over what it called a "calculated political stunt", and said he had ignored guidance to coordinate with Israeli authorities.
"This was not about harvesting olives. It was about harvesting headlines," it said.
The Israeli military said that the Palestinian landowner had not requested permission to conduct the harvest.
"This coordination is necessary to ensure the security of the area and maintain public order," it said, pointing to the "security risk of an uncoordinated harvest" near an Israeli settlement.
Israel has faced growing international criticism over violence during the harvest, with rights groups documenting multiple attacks and other disruptions each day by settlers against Palestinians.
Israel on Monday announced it had made several arrests after settlers beat up a US photojournalist covering the incidents and a French mayor who had come for the olive season.
The violence comes in the final days before Israeli elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has sought to shore up his right-wing base, which is staunchly pro-settlement.
Israel has come under growing fire within the United States, traditionally its top ally.
Lander, who is Jewish, is a close ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, an outspoken critic of Israeli policies.
In a party primary in June, Lander ousted the sitting congressman, Dan Goldman, one of a dwindling number of Democrats who support Israel.--AFP
2f7554dfc8afedca: AUSTRALIA'S security chiefs had warned of "online echo chambers" fuelling grievances and conspiracies and stepped up prosecutions for threats of political violence ahead of Monday's attack on a lawmaker in a rural town.

Independent lawmaker Helen Haines, 65, underwent surgery overnight but remains in a critical condition after being struck deliberately by a car in an attack that "does shake all of us", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday.
Broadcaster ABC and the Sydney Morning Herald reported she had lost a leg.
Brendan Nugent, 43, is in custody after Haines was hit outside her office in Wangaratta, just over 200km northeast of Melbourne.

Police have charged Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a penalty of 10 years in prison.
Police described it as an isolated incident with the motive under investigation by the counter-terrorism team.

Acts of political violence are rare in Australia, and Albanese told the national broadcaster he wanted the country to remain a place where lawmakers can engage with people, go shopping and watch football.
But he said security needed to be "dealt with" amid a significant increase in threats.
Australia's Human Rights Commission said the attack happened "against a backdrop of increasing polarisation and threats against politicians", which could undermine democracy.
Threats against Australian lawmakers and electorate offices doubled between 2021 and last year, with 1,067 incidents reported to police last year.

The Australian Federal Police formed a National Security Investigations team last October, described by police commissioner Krissy Barrett as a "flying squad of hate disruptors", resulting in 41 people being charged for threats against federal politicians, ministers and the prime minister.
Just this month, three men were charged over separate threats to politicians and government officials, and another three were sentenced by courts.

The nation's spy chief, Australian Security Intelligence Organisation director-general Mike Burgess, said last year politically motivated violence was among the agency's fastest growing security concerns, driven by "griev-ance narratives, conspiracies and online echo chambers".
Political intolerance, violent rhetoric and polarisation were also contributing to a "permissive environment of violence", Burg-ess said on Tuesday.
The lawmakers targeted are across the political spectrum and include men.
But the nature of threats directed at female lawmakers is "particularly troubling" because they are targeted because they are women, the federal police said last year.
The University of Melbourne's associate head of psychological sciences, Lisa Phillips, said she was not surprised it was a female lawmaker who had been attacked.
Victoria's state Parliament commissioned Phillips to survey lawmakers on online abuse and stalking five years ago.

"The female politicians who responded almost ubiquitously reported experiences of either unwanted approaches, persistent unwanted contact from people, or experiences of threats or of assault," she said.

05b99ea8d320d9c0: ALEKSA Simic, a political science student at Belgrade University, did not hesitate when he learned that the collapse of a railway station canopy in the northern Serbian city of Novi Sad had killed 16 people in November 2024.

Demanding justice for the dead, and an end to the kind of corruption that many believed led to the station's shoddy construction, he and other students blockaded the political science faculty in protest.
As Serbia mourned, sympathetic residents brought them homemade meals, mattresses and pillows. Many stopped by to discuss the students' demands.
"For the first time, I had a sense of belonging to a community. I realised that my voice mattered," Simic said.

Two years on, as Serbia prepares for elections on Oct 25, the student protest movement has ballooned to become one of the most powerful political forces in the country and poses the greatest threat yet to the rule of Aleksandar Vucic, who has dominated Serbian politics first as prime minister, then president, since 2014.

With protests raging in cities across Europe, fuelled by the high cost of living, a shortage of jobs and poor education standards, the Serbian students have shown what a force younger generations can be when they harness widespread discontent.

In interviews with Reuters, a dozen students and teachers described how a methodical countrywide door-knocking campaign, peaceful marches, a tightly controlled media message and a constant rotation of leaders to protect individuals from government smear campaigns have helped maintain momentum in Serbia.
Now, they have their own "Students Win" list of 250 candidates for Sunday's election, which includes university professors, actors, farmers and even a popular rapper.

The only poll published this month, by New Serbian Political Thought (NSPM) on Oct 20, showed the students' list of candidates edging ahead of Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with 44.5 per cent of the vote to 42.7 per cent, although betting odds favour Vucic.
"The protests changed the society. It showed people they are not alone," said Florian Bieber, professor of Southeast European history and politics at the University of Graz.
The big question is how the students would govern should they win on Sunday.

Vucic is a significant international figure, managing a delicate balancing act that seeks closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union even with the accession process stalled.
The students' list is headed by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, although they have said this does not mean he would become prime minister should they win.

Some political analysts wonder how the country would fare on the international stage with an unknown at the helm, while there are scant details about how the students will set about fulfilling their pledges to fight corruption, promote transparency, create greater media freedom and enact education reform at home.

Critics also point to their silence on joining the EU and relations with the former province of Kosovo. Pro-European opponents of Vucic's government criticise them for saying that they would not introduce sanctions on Russia.

"A (student-led) government would pursue broad reforms to tackle corruption, overhaul key public institutions and companies, and dismantle patronage networks," consultancy Teneo said in an analyst note on Tuesday.
"However, strong bureaucratic resistance could generate short-term institutional instability."
Vucic, 56, stepped down as president in September to run again for prime minister in the snap election.

While he has overseen a period of strong economic growth and a fall in unemployment, critics blame him for democratic backsliding, the silencing of critics and the media, and hampering Serbia's EU accession by not undertaking necessary reforms.
Police have beaten protesters and threatened people who voice opposition online, rights groups, activists and students told Reuters.
Simmering anger towards the government boiled over with the collapse of the station roof in Novi Sad.

Vucic has sought to discredit the student movement, saying it is trying to destroy Serbia and accusing foreign agents from Croatia and Montenegro of financing it, but that has not dented their support.

Vucic and the authorities have repeatedly denied the allegations of corruption and violence and attempts to discredit the opposition. The students dismiss claims that they are being organised from abroad.
The student protests were small to begin with: days after the canopy collapse, a few dozen people blocked traffic in Novi Sad and Belgrade for one minute for each person who was killed.

Less than three months later, in late January 2025, then prime minister and close Vucic ally Milos Vucevic resigned a day after tens of thousands of people blocked one of Belgrade's main junctions, joined by farmers in their tractors.
In March that year, the students led hundreds of thousands of people through Belgrade, the biggest anti-government march in a generation.
By then, the movement had a symbol: a red handprint, representing the blood that the protesters say is on the government's hands.
"We felt we had importance and that we had a greater responsibility," Simic said.
University faculties across the country held plenums and working groups focused on media and social media strategies, and organising marches.
On the first anniversary of the roof collapse, the students walked from Belgrade to Novi Sad. People in small villages offered fruit.

An image of a man with a traditional Serbian hat hugging a Muslim student in a headscarf flooded social media - which supporters hailed as an emblem of a young, progressive Serbia after the devastating Balkan wars of the 1990s.
Ahead of Sunday's vote, student groups have undergone training on election fraud and say teams plan to be present at polling stations.

Gavrilo Andric was a software engineer for a big company when the protests began. An amateur photographer, he watched the movement grow, eventually leaving his job to become its unofficial documenter.
"I finally realised that in our society we have a group of people who see things can be improved and want to work on it together with other people," he told Reuters.

e9890a0f7286e589: OpenBSD 8.0 brings bigger virtual machines, graphics improvements, and another helping of AI mockery. The round version number doesn't signal a radical break with its predecessors.

OpenBSD 8.0 is the 61st release of the project. Developer Bryan Steele posted a highlights rundown on Mastodon. Wireless improvements include updates to the qwx driver for Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6 hardware. Its VMM/VMD hypervisor now supports multiprocessor VMs with up to 64 virtual CPUs in each guest.

The kernel virtual memory address space on x86-64 is now 512 GB, up from 4 GB, allowing for GPUs with large amounts of VRAM. On Arm64 machines, OpenBSD supports hibernation, and on both x86-64 and Arm64 it can use CPU AES instructions for faster encrypted swap.

Component upgrades include OpenSSH 10.6 and LibreSSL 4.4.0, and the DRM graphics driver stack from Linux 6.18. The default C compiler is Clang/LLVM 22, including for the SPARC64 edition – but at the cost of dropping support for the Loongson architecture.

The list of errata is short, with just four fixes – but then, version 8.0 is very new. Just days before this release, there was a high-profile OpenBSD issue: Calif's "Big Fish" research describes a decades-old shared-memory bug chained with a separate kernel flaw to gain local root access. Both were fixed in OpenBSD 7.9, through errata 026 and 018 respectively.

Project leader Theo de Raadt forked OpenBSD from NetBSD 1.0 in 1995, and the first release of the new OS was OpenBSD 1.2 in July 1996 – so version 8.0 is as close as the project will get to a 30th anniversary release. According to Calif's proof-of-concept code on GitHub, the bug was in the original code that both OpenBSD and NetBSD inherited from the original BSD codebase – which is how come there's a 37-year-old bug in a 30-year-old project. A HackerNews comment says: "Interestingly, looks like this was accidentally fixed in NetBSD during a rewrite of that code in August of 1999."
The project has not updated its infamous slogan. The homepage still proclaims: "Only two remote holes in the default install, in a heck of a long time!"

As we noted in May when OpenBSD 7.9 appeared, the project rejects code generated by LLMs, although on the basis of licensing concerns rather than its cousin NetBSD's explicit anti-AI stance. As we reported recently, this strict anti-AI stance seems to be serving NetBSD well.

OpenBSD is also an anti-AI project, and for this release, the website goes out of its way to make that very clear. OpenBSD's mascot is a pufferfish, and in the banner artwork for the new release, "Puffy" has an extra eye – and the signpost in the image's background also has malformed text, a hallmark of early image-generation bots. The eyes are also constantly blinking – one at a time – to emphasize that this is a reference to Blinky the mutant fish from The Simpsons. In case you missed The Simpsons reference, the version 8.0 release theme song makes it even more explicit: it's titled "The Simps on AI." The lyrics and the vocals parody both Simpsons characters and AI users. Our favorite line sounds like Grampa Simpson, and says:
Back in my day we didn't have artificial intelligence, we had real stupidity – and we liked it.

We've seen negative reactions online, but then we often find that some people lack much of a sense of humor. For our part, we really enjoyed seeing the OpenBSD team having such fun. We reckon it will appeal to many Butlerian Jihadi types. It certainly did to The Reg FOSS desk.
A little Wine with your pufferfish
A couple of days before the 8.0 release came an unexpected announcement on the openbsd-ports mailing list: a proposed port of Wine for OpenBSD.

This is a new version of the Wine 11 runtime that allows Windows binaries to launch and run on OpenBSD. This is a 64-bit version of Wine for OpenBSD on x86-64, and for now, this means it can only run 64-bit Windows code.

(For the technical nitty-gritty: Wine needs to manipulate the CPU's GS register. Windows on x86-64 uses the GS segment base to locate the Thread Environment Block (TEB), as the late great Geoff Chappell explained. This is a very longstanding Windows data structure, going all the way back through Windows 95 to OS/2. The port was particularly tricky because OpenBSD doesn't allow programs to alter that, so the port is emulating instructions that use the %gs segment override. The snags are that this means 32-bit code doesn't work, and secondly, because this is unnecessary on Linux, the code is unlikely to be merged back into upstream Wine.)

If you want to see it working, there are a few screenshot galleries on Reddit's openbsd_gaming group, showing a number of recent major titles running: Some samples from WIP wine port, more wine-on-OpenBSD screenshots, and even more wine-on-OpenBSD proof.

The port comes hedged with caveats, notable among them that Wine does not do any kind of sandboxing, so using it potentially opens up OpenBSD to Windows malware. However, for some users, this could be a very useful addition.

OpenBSD is the simplest and cleanest member of the BSD family, indeed, of the FOSS Unix family. Part of this is because entire subsystems are missing that the other BSDs provide. Bluetooth connections to Apple's wireless keyboards and pointing devices aren't supported. There's no logical volume management – which would massively help with OpenBSD's complex disk partitioning. There's no journaling filesystem either (although a port of the new Gefs is in progress). While small and clean, its priorities favor security and simplicity, though performance will depend on the hardware and workload.
Importantly – since you probably will need to ask for help – the OpenBSD community does not have a reputation for friendliness.

Saying that, it is quite a lot easier to get OpenBSD installed and running, complete with its 25-year-old version 2.2.5 of the Fvwm window manager, than either NetBSD or FreeBSD. If you're looking for an AI-free, and indeed systemd-free, path away from Linux, OpenBSD 8.0 is very definitely worth a try. ®
08fd9e9d10a029a3: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 72 Malaysians were detained overseas on suspicion of drug-related offences from January to Oct 15, with 1,704kg of drugs worth RM81.76 million seized.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said 48 cases were recorded, involving 57 men and 15 women.

Thailand recorded the highest number of arrests at 19, followed by Indonesia (16), Taiwan and Singapore (eight each), Japan (five), the Philippines (four), India and Hong Kong (three each), Macau (two), and South Korea, Nigeria, the Maldives and Sri Lanka (one each).
Hussein said international drug syndicates could be exploiting Malaysians as drug couriers through job offers, lucrative rewards, sponsored travel and requests to deliver goods for third parties.
"Such tactics could deceive individuals who are unaware of the risks and legal implications, exposing them to severe legal action in the countries concerned," he said in a statement.

Among the cases was the detention of five Malaysians at Haneda Airport in Tokyo on Oct 10 for allegedly attempting to smuggle about 5kg of cocaine worth RM3.1 million. Malaysians had also been detained in drug-related cases in Macau and Singapore.
Hussein said drug trafficking and smuggling could carry severe penalties, including the death penalty in some countries, depending on the offence, the quantity of drugs and the applicable laws.
He urged the public, particularly youths, students and those planning to travel overseas, to be wary of suspicious job offers, free travel and promises of lucrative rewards.

ebe891935f169822: PETALING JAYA: The PAS-led Kelantan government has sidestepped calls to drop the sole Bersatu representative from the state executive council.

4f53d719624d40c1: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is continuing to disburse financial assistance in stages under the Paddy Crop Takaful Scheme (STTP) to registered farmers affected by drought this year.
The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM) said RM1.99 million had been paid in stages to farmers in areas under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA) from June until this month.
Another RM5.13 million in aid for farmers outside Mada areas will be distributed in stages from Oct 23.

"The welfare of padi farmers remains a priority for the government, including addressing the effects of drought and delays in fertiliser supplies in Mada areas," the ministry said in a statement today.
On the delays in fertiliser supplies in Mada areas, the ministry said any assessment of their impact on padi production must be based on actual yield data rather than assumptions.

It said a preliminary analysis of 21 per cent of samples from Mada's Crop Cutting Survey (CCS) estimated the average gross yield for Season 1/2026 at 5.69 tonnes per hectare, compared with 4.60 tonnes per hectare in Season 1/2025.
"These preliminary findings show an increase in average gross yield across Mada and, so far, do not indicate an overall decline in yields.
"However, the figures are still preliminary and cannot be regarded as a definitive conclusion on the impact of fertiliser supply delays on individual farmers," it said.
The ministry said a comprehensive study would be conducted after harvesting was completed in November to obtain a more complete and accurate picture of padi production for the season.
It said any conclusions and follow-up measures must be objective, evidence-based and take into account farmers' interests and the sustainability of national padi production.
The ministry added that it would continue monitoring developments on the ground and ensure farmers' welfare remained a priority while safeguarding rice supply stability and national food security.
77d06fe1ce7d20bb: PETALING JAYA: A 16-year-old teenager who allegedly attacked a teacher with an axe at Tunku Putra-HELP International School (TPH) in Kuching this morning livestreamed the incident on social media, police said.

0ddda4543527f4f6: WASHINGTON: OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled or weakened systems built to catch them misbehaving, with one later denying it had done so.
The cases are the latest in a string of safety scares at the world's top AI developers involving agents, AI programmes that carry out tasks without human involvement.

In a report released Tuesday, the ChatGPT maker said that during two internal coding jobs, its agents switched off or undermined tools for detecting incidents of AI models acting against human wishes.

On Oct 3, an agent running on OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol model, which had been told not to send any messages on the workplace chat app, took that as licence to switch off safety alerts meant for the company's security team while fixing a testing system.
Three days later, a GPT-6 Astra agent stripped out its own monitor while copying code from another project, then told the human programmer it had done no such thing.
The company said it had also seen several cases of agents launching software with monitoring switched off, exposing a gap in its oversight.
OpenAI said it is still trying to determine whether the models were simply overzealous in following instructions or have a particular tendency to evade monitoring.
"We don't yet have a satisfying explanation for this behaviour," it said.
The disclosure adds to mounting unease over how well leading labs can control increasingly autonomous systems.

In July, a group of OpenAI agents broke out of their test environments and launched a cyberattack on AI firm Hugging Face, causing international alarm. Other companies have since reported similar incidents.
The incidents have fuelled calls in the United States and abroad for tighter oversight of AI development.
But US President Donald Trump, under the advice of top AI executives like Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, has urged the industry to police itself.

a25875e508ad8e84: Nearly two-thirds of US doctors are turning to an AI-powered search engine to make patient decisions, propelling a little-known tech startup to a $15 billion valuation while prompting a debate over the future of patient care.

68b71cea051e87bc: KUALA LUMPUR: Winning the Queen Elizabeth II Commonwealth Trust 100 Young Leaders Award has encouraged three young people to continue their work supporting underserved communities through healthcare, education and technology.

52842e009da6f020: PHP developers have released emergency updates for two critical vulnerabilities after cybersecurity authorities warned organizations to patch immediately or consider taking exposed applications offline.
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 address CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The project's developers urged users to update immediately.

All PHP installations serving web requests are potentially affected, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache's mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, the developers said. "We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs."

Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at watchTowr, said: "As expected, watchTowr Intel is already observing in-the-wild exploitation of the latest PHP vulnerabilities, with a variety of vibecoded PoCs already hitting our sensors featuring a variety of 'php2shell' User-Agents. Whilst nobody has been successful to date, we don't expect that will last long."

"Where immediate patching is not feasible, organizations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available," CERT-EU said in an advisory issued ahead of the patches. The body lists both vulnerabilities with CVSS scores of 9.2.

Finnish government services and websites belonging to the Dutch parliament, cybersecurity authorities, and data protection regulator were taken offline as a precaution. Privacy campaign group noyb also temporarily withdrew its website.

PHP "powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," infosec vendor Huntress noted.

That makes identifying exposed installations a substantial job. "The number of places you have to go looking to identify vulnerable PHP versions gets very big, very fast," said John Hammond, Huntress's senior principal security researcher. ®

0d1c59b202fa5211: GENEVA: The El Nino weather phenomenon gripping the planet is heading off the charts, the UN warned Wednesday, saying countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.
El Nino is set to peak in December, but the human impact of its associated extreme temperatures, floods and droughts is set to last into 2027 and beyond.
The UN called for international preventative measures to protect the millions of people most exposed – before disaster strikes.

"The current El Nino event could be unprecedented in strength: literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades," said Celeste Saulo, head of the UN's weather and climate agency.

"We are already witnessing extreme weather events and expect this to multiply and cascade as El Nino intensifies," the World Meteorological Organization chief told a press conference in Geneva, alongside UN aid chief Tom Fletcher.
They issued a joint call for "urgent and coordinated anticipatory action" to protect the most vulnerable communities already living on the edge.
"We cannot stop El Nino, but we can prevent many of its worst human consequences," said Saulo.
'Wrecking ball'
Fletcher said El Nino was a "wrecking ball" that would bring havoc to Latin America, eastern and southern Africa, Asia and the Pacific.
He said the long-term impact "will be felt for months and potentially years to come... because it's this overlaying of crisis on crisis and crisis".
He cited widespread conflict and displacement, soaring fuel and fertiliser and food prices, and swingeing aid cuts.
"The risk is you have tens of millions of people pushed into humanitarian need," he explained, warning that 50 million people could face increased hunger.
Fletcher said the next two weeks were "the critical window to act".

Somalia, Ethiopia, and Kenya need supplies ahead of heavy rains; southern Africa needs seeds and livestock. Central America needs livelihood assistance, while Asia and the Pacific must prepare for droughts, floods and cyclones, he said.
However, Fletcher warned that the damage from El Nino would not be limited to countries on the front line.
"It will create economic shocks for the global economy and drive further conflict, displacement, migration," he said.
"I am sounding the alarm that the humanitarian system... cannot alone cope with a threat on this scale."
He called on countries, development banks and international financial institutions to get money moving "before that damage is done".
Fletcher said he had released US$50 million to help 11 countries on the frontline, including Chad, El Salvador, Ethiopia, Somalia and South Sudan.
'Far-reaching consequences'
El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.
It typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.
The naturally occurring weather phenomenon is set to bring higher temperatures to much of the planet, with its impact compounding the effects of man-made climate change.

The WMO's latest global seasonal climate update out Wednesday forecasted that sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean – the epicentre of El Nino – may rise to 3.8°C above average during November to January: way above typical El Nino figures.
This would be the highest three-month measurement since observations began, eclipsing the previous record of 2.6°C set in 2015-2016.
"This will have far-reaching consequences for weather patterns across the world," said Saulo.
While El Nino usually peaks between November and February, the resulting spike in temperatures typically comes later.
The last El Nino contributed to making 2023 the second-hottest year on record and 2024 the all-time high.
This El Nino is already hitting some regions hard, including in Central America, where animals and crops are dying from drought.

Dzulkefly said a task force established by the public services department in April was looking into staffing issues, while the ministry had been given greater authority to manage and distribute approved positions to speed up recruitment.
Dzulkefly said six government hospitals had met a target of treating at least 70% of non-emergency patients within two hours, compared with the average waiting time of four to six hours previously.
In a written reply to Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (Ind-Tanjong Karang), he said Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital in Ipoh recorded the highest rate with 98.61% of green zone patients treated within two hours.

This was followed by Ampang Hospital (88.78%), Selayang Hospital (74.1%), Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Bahru (73.2%), Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital in Klang (72.2%) and Kuala Lumpur Hospital (71.8%).
He also highlighted a 9% reduction in patient attendance at six major hospitals following the extension of operating hours at selected government health clinics.
The clinics operate until 9pm on weekdays and from 8am to 1pm on weekends and public holidays.
The extended hours had helped divert patients with minor ailments from hospital emergency departments, he said.
Dzulkefly also said all eight initiatives under the special task force on agency reform to reduce hospital overcrowding had been fully implemented as of June.

Other measures include outsourcing treatment to private general practitioners, expanding digital screening for non-emergency patients before they visit clinics to 545 health clinics, and improving patient flow at government hospitals.
65c4c44041192d4a: Cute robots stole the show at Nvidia's GTC keynote in Berlin, where Jensen Huang pitched a future powered by AI agents – and, naturally, plenty of his company's hardware.
The Nvidia chief remained his usual ebullient self despite environmental protesters interrupting his presentation at Berlin's tent-shaped Tempodrom.
"Why don't you clean up your act?" they demanded, holding up banners that partially obscured the presentation screen behind Huang.
"All important issues, but let me get through my keynote," he joked, adding: "I'll talk to you guys later," as security swiftly removed them.
Huang was discussing Vera Rubin systems before unveiling DSX POD, a reference design for factory-built, containerized AI infrastructure.

DSX POD combines seven liquid-cooled Vera Rubin compute racks using Nvidia's Spectrum-X networking. Partners will cable, integrate, and test the systems in modular containers before delivery, with availability expected in early 2027.

Nvidia claims deployment could shrink from six months to as little as 14 days at a prepared site. That excludes the not insignificant matter of getting power, connectivity, and other site infrastructure ready first.

He was keen to add that Vera Rubin systems are designed for closed-loop liquid cooling with coolant temperatures up to 45°C, while outdoor dry coolers release heat into the air without needing to evaporate water. "At 2 gigawatts, DSX can save 54 million litres of water a day," Huang claimed, perhaps thinking of those environmental protesters.
Yet much of the leather-jacketed leader's attention was focused on physical AI: robots, autonomous vehicles, and other machinery Nvidia hopes to supply with its hardware and software.

The Microducks from Pollen Robotics are small, two-legged robots with cameras for faces. Huang interacted with them on stage, getting them to lie down and roll over by voice command, and the little robots all beeped back at him in response.
The robo ducks demonstrated a workflow in which AI was trained in the cloud, evaluated on an Nvidia RTX Spark PC, then deployed on the robots.

Huang also unveiled Agile ONE SN, a humanoid robot reference platform from German robotics startup Agile Robots, based on Nvidia's Isaac GR00T technology and a Jetson Thor compute module. Scheduled for early 2027, the platform is intended to give robotics researchers and developers a ready-made system for developing and testing capabilities.
"This is going to be the next major industry, the next great industry," Huang claimed.

Beyond robots, Nvidia is pushing its AI hardware and software into cars and telecoms networks. Huang boasted that Nvidia's Hyperion car system is being adopted by more vendors, saying: "We turned this into an industry standard, and now it's being designed into one car fleet after another."

Europe's telecoms operators are also deploying Nvidia-powered computing in their networks to deliver advanced services using AI-RAN, according to Huang. "After working on this for nearly eight years, Nvidia made the first commercial phone call on the T-Mobile network with Nokia, and so now CUDA makes phone calls," he said.
Far from slowing down the progression of AI, it seems Nvidia is determined to push its technology into every corner of the world. "Everyone will become an AI company," Huang claimed.

He also took care to praise Europe and its technology efforts while he was in Berlin. "As expected, Jensen positioned Nvidia as a strong supporter of – and enabler for – Europe's sovereign tech ambitions. Nvidia has invested almost $10 billion into Europe in the past year, including 14 investments into European startups during Jensen's current trip," said Forrester principal analyst Paul Miller.

But Miller pointed out that Nvidia itself is not European. "Anything with critical ongoing dependencies on Nvidia (or any other non-European firm) is unlikely to meet the purest definitions of European tech sovereignty," he added.
Huang closed with a CGI video of robots performing a Eurovision-style song recapping his keynote. Yes, it was as bad as you imagine. ®
6f6ef0f42c2350fe: An ‘all British, all day’ station is a nativist dream come true – but good luck with the playlist. And anyway: how many artists will want to be on Farage FM? Two months before Margaret Thatcher became prime minister in May 1979, a national Militant Entertainment Tour was organised by Rock Against Racism. On 20 March 1979, it came to the West Runton Pavilion near Cromer, the (very) small town on the coastal edge of East Anglia. The bill mixed the black and white musicians in three bands then at their artistic peak – the post-punk maestros Gang of Four, the punk-reggae hybridists The Ruts, and Misty in Roots, the renowned reggae collective from Southall in west London – and thereby made a stark symbolic point: that the multiracial nature of large swathes of the UK was not to be decried or attacked, but actively celebrated. ad664e1aa397da2d: PETALING JAYA: Remaja dipercayai menyerang seorang guru menggunakan kapak di Sekolah Antarabangsa Tunku Putra-HELP (TPH) hari ini bukannya pelajar aktif institusi itu.
TPH berkata, pelajar itu kini dalam tahanan polis susulan serangan pagi tadi.

TPH berkata, guru wanita itu tidak mengalami kecederaan kritikal dan kini dalam keadaan stabil serta semakin pulih selepas mendapatkan rawatan di hospital.

Menurutnya, tiga anggota polis bantuan akan ditempatkan di kawasan sekolah serta-merta dan pemeriksaan keselamatan bersesuaian akan dijalankan terhadap individu yang memasuki kawasan sekolah.

61bdc60666d52a48: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has asked the public to stop transferring money into his personal bank account, saying he does not want to feel guilty over their generosity.
He said he had received RM45,102.18 from well-wishers seeking to help him pay RM300,000 in damages and costs after losing a defamation suit filed by DAP veteran Teresa Kok.
In a Facebook post today, Akmal apologised for removing the bank account number he had shared in an earlier post.
"I ask that no more money be deposited into the account so that I do not feel guilty towards everyone.
"This is because almost everyone transferring money into my account is doing so not to buy the motorcycle or tilapia fish, but to contribute to me.
"As of this statement, I have received RM45,102.18, and I am very grateful.
"However, my intention was to try to sell my assets first, namely my motorcycle and fish," he said.
Akmal said he did not want to burden anyone by asking for financial assistance and would take full responsibility for the payment.
"It is fine, I will bear it. I only need prayers from all of you.
"So, to anyone who wants to buy the Honda X-ADV motorcycle, I will provide the details after this and you can message me directly," he said.
On Monday, the Melaka High Court ruled in favour of Kok in her defamation suit against Akmal, ordering him to pay RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages, along with RM50,000 in costs.

The suit concerned remarks Akmal made about Kok in a TikTok video in September 2024, after she criticised a proposal to make halal certification mandatory for eateries that do not serve pork or alcohol.

The court also ordered Akmal to remove the video from his social media accounts within seven days and barred him from publishing or broadcasting the defamatory statements, or words to the same effect.
5d50bdb9f42e99c2: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) lacks the manpower needed to optimally manage the country's borders, home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today.
Saifuddin said the agency was still strengthening its organisation after taking over the border control role from various agencies, including the immigration department and the customs department.
"As of Sept 23, AKPS had 8,403 personnel, a number seen as insufficient for optimal operations in managing all of the country's 123 entry points," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
He said the home ministry was creating and filling new posts, prioritising operations at entry points with higher risks, traffic, and cargo.
These posts would be filled in phases over the next five years.
The agency was also rationalising and optimising personnel deployment based on risk factors and actual operational needs to ensure efficient use of human resources without affecting border security.
"AKPS is also continuing to work with other core agencies in this transition period, including for operational coordination, resource sharing and enforcement support as needed," he said.
He was replying to Khlir Nor (Bersatu-Ketereh), who asked about the ministry's measures to address AKPS's manpower shortage.
AKPS was allocated 8,403 positions at its launch.
07fabd2b021c86e0: SEREMBAN: Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negri Sembilan (DKU) secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin and DKU have applied to intervene in an originating summons filed by 10 former Negri Sembilan executive council (exco) members over the interpretation of the State Constitution.
High Court Judge Roz Mawar Rozain fixed Nov 2 to hear the application and directed all parties to file their respective written submissions by Oct 30. The hearing will be conducted via Zoom at 11 am.

The court also fixed Nov 16 to hear a preliminary objection by the Negri Sembilan State Secretary and the state government, the respondents in the case, challenging the use of the originating summons to initiate the proceedings.
They contend that the matter should instead have been brought through judicial review.
The notice of preliminary objection must be filed by Oct 23, with written submissions due on Nov 10 and replies by Nov 13.

During today's proceedings, the court was informed that the 10 applicants had filed an application in the Federal Court on Oct 14 seeking a reference on questions concerning the interpretation of provisions in the Negri Sembilan State Constitution under Article 34(2).
The Federal Court has fixed a case management session via e-review on Oct 23.
The High Court judge said the intervention applications must be disposed of before the court could determine the next steps in the proceedings.
Lawyer Datuk Mohd Hafarizam Harun, representing the 10 applicants, said he needed to obtain instructions from his clients on whether they would oppose the intervention applications.
The court also directed the applicants to file any affidavit in reply by Oct 26 should they decide to oppose the applications.

Meanwhile, lawyer Datuk Dr Cyrus Das, representing the Negri Sembilan State Secretary, said his clients had no objection to the court hearing the intervention applications first to facilitate the orderly progress of the proceedings.
The originating summons also includes a claim for damages by the plaintiffs.
On Sept 20, the Negri Sembilan palace announced that the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had revoked the appointments of the exco members with immediate effect.
The revocation of their appointments was gazetted on Sept 24, with their removal effective from Sept 20.

The gazette stated that their appointments were revoked and annulled because they violated their pledge of allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz when they agreed on Tuanku Muhriz's removal as the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
e0460d6b5c061f18: PETALING JAYA: The investigation paper on Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Ismail Lasim's claim that he was coerced into signing a proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang Dipertuan Besar is with the Attorney-General's Chambers.
Home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said police took the statements of four people to assist in the probe, and that the investigation paper was submitted to the AGC on Sept 29.
"The police are waiting for the AGC's decision and further instructions concerning the investigation paper.

"Any action and further investigation by the police is subject to the AGC's instructions. The police will take necessary action according to the relevant legal provisions," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
Saifuddin was responding to Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah) who asked for the latest status of the investigation into the police report filed by Ismail on Sept 8.

On Sept 5, the four disputed undangs, or chieftains, claimed that Ismail had signed the proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz, although the menteri besar sidestepped the allegation and declared full loyalty to the ruler.
Three days later, the undangs produced the purported proclamation signed by Ismail at a press conference.

a4f21b6be9a03849: NEW YORK: Wall Street stocks opened higher Wednesday after a string of well-received earnings reports, with SpaceX's first profit reassuring investors about the financial outlook for the artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem.
In early trading, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.34%, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.67% and the broad-based S&P 500 added 0.31%.
"We have a market where a lot of the negative factors that were holding the market down over the last few weeks are being alleviated," Adam Sarhan of 50 Park Investments told AFP.
He pointed to easing bond yields and expectations that inflation is slowing, helped in part by cheaper agricultural commodities.
"Even gasoline prices have come down a lot over the last few weeks," he said.
"That means that whole fear that the Fed is going to raise rates and choke the economy and the stock market is going away."
AI and rocket giant SpaceX was in demand at the open, a day after posting quarterly results seen as encouraging, including a first profit of US$4.4 billion.
In early trading, Elon Musk's company rose 8.36% to US$160.15. The stock nonetheless remains well below the highs of around US$225 it reached in June.
"SpaceX is definitely a good sign because a big piece of their business right now is AI related and it is growing very fast," Sarhan said.
"So we're starting to get a relief rally in a lot of these AI stocks that were just... beaten down a lot."
f36a4fc538a1eb72: PETALING JAYA: Barisan Nasional (BN) akan bertanding di 21 kerusi pada PRN Melaka akan datang, manakala PAS dan 'rakan-rakan' akan bertanding di tujuh kerusi, kata Pengerusi BN Zahid Hamidi.

74b6052ee464197b: RANTAU PANJANG: A Kelantan policeman who was seriously injured in a parang attack during an anti-drug operation last week has vowed to continue fighting drug abuse following the seven-year jail sentence imposed on his attacker.
The corporal requested anonymity over concerns for his safety and that of his family.
He said he was grateful for and satisfied with the court's decision after the labourer was sentenced to seven years in prison and two strokes of the rotan by the Pasir Mas Sessions Court today.
"I am very grateful to learn that the suspect has been sentenced. I am satisfied with the court's decision over what happened to me.
"My spirit in fighting drugs has never wavered," said the father of two when met at his home.
Earlier, the 37-year-old corporal received a visit from Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat and other officers.
Yusoff said the suspect was a drug user and not a member of a drug smuggling syndicate.
"The suspect consumed yaba pills and ketum juice and has six previous records involving drug-related offences," he said.

The corporal sustained serious injuries, including a fracture to his left arm, after he was attacked with a parang while pursuing a suspected drug offender during an operation at Kampung Lalang Pepuyu, Tanah Merah, on Oct 17.

The incident occurred at 1.35pm when a team from the Kelantan police contingent's Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, assisted by personnel from the Bukit Bunga and Lalang Pepuyu police stations, raided a house in the village.
The suspect, Muhammad Syahid Che Mat, 30, allegedly attempted to flee while carrying a parang.
He then swung the weapon at officers attempting to apprehend him, leaving the corporal seriously injured.
Syahid pleaded guilty to causing grievous hurt to the policeman using a dangerous weapon.
The court ordered the prison sentence to take effect from the date of his arrest on Oct 17.
e3c517dafc36dcd2: PETALING JAYA: Barisan Nasional has confirmed that it will contest 21 of the 28 seats up for grabs in the Nov 14 Melaka state election, with PAS and its allies to vie for the remaining seven.
BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also the Umno president, said the coalition will form an alliance with PAS and its partners from the deregistered Perikatan Nasional for the Melaka polls.

668723f89f712103: SAINT PETERSBURG: The Ukrainian and European approaches to ending the war in Ukraine that US envoy Steve Witkoff relayed to President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday lacked much substance, the Kremlin said.
The Kremlin added that Russia was ready to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US in November.
Witkoff held more than three hours of talks with Putin in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday, as Washington seeks to reinvigorate long-stalled efforts aimed at ending the Ukraine war.
The conflict, which is grinding through its fifth year, has become Europe's deadliest since World War II.

"Steve Witkoff briefed Vladimir Putin on the substance of the talks held in Oslo," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters, referring to talks Witkoff held in Norway with Ukrainian and European officials on Tuesday.
"He mentioned some new aspects in the approaches of the Europeans and Kyiv... but there wasn't really much substance in them."
"Our president informed Steve Witkoff that we are, in principle, ready to resume the mentioned (trilateral) talks," he added, saying they could take place in mid-November.
These talks would focus on "building security ... after the end of the conflict," Ushakov added.
d92b38ab12e76ae1: TAIPEI: Five people in Taiwan were charged on Wednesday for allegedly attacking a Taiwanese stand-up comedian after he criticised the Chinese Communist Party, prosecutors said.

Taiwan has accused China of growing transnational repression targeting critics on the island, which Beijing claims is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to bring it under its control.

The Taiwanese defendants were allegedly hired by a Chinese person to surveil and assault Huang Yi-hao to prevent him from performing at a show on Sept 20, the New Taipei Prosecutors Office said in a statement.
The five began tracking Huang in July and planned to stage a car accident with the intention of breaking his arms and legs so he would be hospitalised and unable to go on stage, the prosecutors said.
Two of the defendants allegedly rammed a car into Huang's scooter as he rode home on Sept 11, leaving him with a bruised pelvis.

"This case involves a serious incident in which the Chinese Communist Party is suspected of using cross-border suppression tactics to direct lawless elements in our country to suppress dissenting political voices through extreme violence," the prosecutors said.
Two of the defendants have admitted their involvement in the plan to injure Huang, they said.

The five "willingly served foreign hostile forces with the intent to create a chilling effect" in Taiwanese society, prosecutors said, adding that the attack showed "extreme malice" and "disregard for human life."
After the incident, the defendants obtained Huang's medical records in order to request the final instalment of the NT$450,000 (US$13,900) payment from the Chinese national.
Huang thanked investigators and warned that freedom of speech would be at risk if China ever ruled Taiwan.

"All I did was spend two and a half minutes criticising (Chinese President) Xi Jinping on a stage in Taiwan, yet I was subsequently targeted with both a faeces-throwing attack and a deliberate vehicular assault," Huang said in a statement on Facebook.

"If people can already be subjected to this kind of treatment simply for criticising the Chinese Communist Party when it does not even govern Taiwan, how can we expect to retain our current freedom of speech if the CCP were ever to rule Taiwan?"--AFP
4631a9a8dfbc8e9e: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan Kelantan akan memilih pendekatan terbaik berhubung kedudukan exco daripada Bersatu, di sebalik gesaan supaya kedudukan mereka dikaji semula.
Timbalan Menteri Besar Fadzli Hassan berkata kerajaan Kelantan sedang mengikuti perkembangan di peringkat pusat dan negeri.

Terdahulu, Naib Presiden Parti Wawasan Negara, Wan Saiful Wan Jan, menggesa kedudukan wakil rakyat Bersatu yang dilantik sebagai exco di Kedah, Kelantan dan Terengganu dikaji semula.

Gesaan itu menyusuli tindakan Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM) membatalkan pendaftaran Perikatan Nasional, ekoran aduan Bersatu yang menurut setiausaha agung parti itu berkenaan pelanggaran perlembagaan oleh kepimpinan baharu PN.

fa7bb17084be0a6b: BERLIN: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed Wednesday that the EU would defend itself against what he called "unfair" Chinese trade practices that could threaten German industry.

The leader of Europe's biggest economy, who is set to travel next week to Singapore, Japan and South Korea, criticised Chinese industrial overcapacities, subsidies for products and export advantages that he said came from an artificially cheap currency.
"We want to have fair trade with China in our joint and mutual interest. That is our goal," Merz said at a Berlin conference.
"But at the same time, we have to be ready to defend ourselves, to defend our industry."
Germany – home to industrial giants in the auto, chemicals and electronics sectors – long prided itself on a massive trade surplus with the rest of the world, including booming sales to China.
That has turned in recent years, however, as Chinese firms have become increasingly competitive and German exporters have been hit by rising production costs and US tariffs.
In recent months, EU leaders including Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron have seriously weighed new policy moves to protect EU-based industry from Chinese competition.
Merz said recent talks by EU officials with China had made some progress, including an agreement to reduce the number of cars exported to the European market.
He said the moves "are not the beginning of a trade war with China".
"But we will also protect our industry with a new set of EU trade defence instruments, because in sustainable trade relations, one side shouldn't profit at the expense of the other," Merz said.
"Germany, France and the entire EU (have) now come to the point where they are ready to defend their interests and that's what we are doing," he said.
Merz noted that China's total trade surplus with the EU was well over €300 billion (US$337 billion) each year.
He said some of China's success was due to strong new companies and excellent research, adding that "we have to respect that".
He also acknowledged that structural problems in Europe had created problems for the German economy and weighed on exports.
"But this is also due to overcapacities, high subsidies on the automotive sector and others and... an artificially under-valued currency" in China, Merz added. "This has to be addressed."
While Merz is travelling elsewhere in Asia next week, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, who holds a largely ceremonial post, will visit China next week.
Steinmeier's office said he plans to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping during the first visit to China by a German president since 2018.
fd092f48e2fb8fcb: LANGKAWI: All 251 passengers and 10 crew members aboard the Express Bahagia 98 ferry were safely evacuated after the vessel ran aground on a sandbar near the Kuala Perlis Passenger Jetty Terminal.

Consortium Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd operations manager Lieutenant Commander Norhafiz Abdul Wahid said the ferry departed Langkawi at 9.30am and became stranded near Buoy No. 1 while approaching Kuala Perlis at 10.35am.

The incident is believed to have occurred when the captain tried to avoid fishing nets stretched across the navigation channel. Both main engines stopped during the manoeuvre, and strong winds pushed the vessel towards the sandbar, Norhafiz said.
Initial attempts to tow the ferry using Feri Kenangan 6 and the Langkawi Auto Express 1 roll-on/roll-off ferry failed because of the receding tide, he said.
The evacuation was carried out using boats from the Marine Police, the Kuala Perlis Fishermen Association and a private company.
All 251 passengers and their luggage were safely transferred to the jetty by about 2.50pm, after the ferry had been stranded for about four hours and 15 minutes, Norhafiz said.

389c9bdf4b715e22: PETALING JAYA: Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman has denied targeting Indonesia as a nation in his call for Asean to exert pressure over the recurring transboundary haze, saying action should be taken against companies responsible for forest fires regardless of their domicile.

22142f8e91cd1525: Microsoft is raising OneDrive's supported macOS sync limit to one million items, matching Windows, alongside new Copilot features, sharing controls, and an admin command-line tool.

The macOS preview is scheduled for the Insiders ring this month, with general availability targeted for June 2027. Eligible devices must meet hardware and configuration requirements; others retain the existing 300,000-item supported limit.
"This increase is intended to help organizations with large OneDrive and SharePoint libraries sync more content reliably across devices," Microsoft said.

However, sync performance may suffer for large numbers of read-only files or accounts under legal hold. "We are actively working to improve performance and reliability for these scenarios," Microsoft said.
Microsoft's cull of OneDrive's File Explorer shortcuts wasn't a retreat from AI. Its latest announcement gives Copilot more to do.

The assistant can now be asked to analyze across files (for example, selecting several spreadsheets and getting the bot to come up with charts and graphs), told to organize folders, or save a repeated workflow as a personal skill in a Markdown file. There is also a Prompt Gallery to save the user from having to come up with their own ideas.

Perhaps most interesting is the addition of "Hero Links," designed to end the proliferation of links to files and folders in OneDrive as permission needs change. The feature provides one link per file and folder by default, with permissions that can be updated while keeping the same URL.
Automatic expiration controls are still coming, however. Organizations that require time-limited access will want to check that gap before adopting the feature.

Administrators also get a OneDrive Sync command-line tool, available in private preview, for inspecting accounts, configuration, policies, and sync status. The tool can pull information from the OneDrive sync client and provide data on status, policy troubleshooting, and issue diagnosis, from folder backup and policy problems on a single PC to identifying devices that need attention across an organization.
And yes, there is, of course, integration with AI agents. ®
c9e5c44c52943092: SEPANG: After spending 12 years in prison in Malaysia, Filipino national Alma Nudo Atenza left the country today after having become the central figure in a landmark ruling that reshaped the law on drug-trafficking prosecutions.
Alma, 60, was arrested at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Aug 19, 2014, after arriving from Hong Kong with 2,556.4g of methamphetamine.
She was convicted of drug trafficking by the Shah Alam High Court and sentenced to death.
Her case took a historic turn when it reached the Federal Court.
In April 2019, a nine-member bench led by then chief justice Richard Malanjum struck down Section 37A of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 as unconstitutional.
The provision allowed the prosecution to rely on two successive statutory presumptions to establish a drug-trafficking charge, easing its burden of proving guilt.

The Federal Court ruled that the double-presumption mechanism violated Article 5(1) of the Federal Constitution, which guarantees personal liberty, read together with Article 8(1), which guarantees equality before the law.
The decision strengthened constitutional safeguards for accused persons by restricting the use of successive presumptions to secure convictions in serious criminal cases.
However, the ruling did not legalise drug trafficking or invalidate other presumptions under the Act. It struck down only the provision allowing the use of two successive presumptions.
Following the ruling, Alma’s death sentence was commuted to 18 years’ imprisonment, backdated to the day of her arrest.
She was released early after receiving a one-third remission of her sentence.
Speaking through her lawyer, A Srimurugan, at the departure hall of KLIA Terminal 2, Alma thanked the officers at Kajang prison for looking after her during her incarceration.
She also expressed regret over her actions and said she hoped to reunite with her son, who was expected to meet her upon her arrival in Manila tonight.
d7527620a046d8d7: ATHENS: Thousands of students and teachers took to the streets across Greece on Wednesday, demanding higher state funding for education, better facilities and less-crowded classrooms, echoing protesters in other European countries.

About 10,000 demonstrators, including school and university students, rallied peacefully in central Athens and suburbs, police said. Others joined rallies in cities across the country, all voicing their solidarity with growing protests in France and elsewhere in Europe over soaring living costs and over what they called crumbling school conditions.

The protests add pressure on prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis' centre-right government, which faces elections in mid-2027, as Greeks struggle with stagnant wages, high rents and rising energy costs years after the country's debt crisis.

"From Greece to France, we want public, free education," protesters chanted as they gathered outside parliament. Students had set up tents in central Athens' Syntagma Square and staged an overnight protest before Wednesday's march.
State school and hospital operations were disrupted as some primary school teachers and doctors walked out, protesting over pay and staff shortages.

Education Minister Sofia Zacharaki said before the protests that she was hearing students' demands. She acknowledged housing costs were putting pressure on Greek households and said projects worth more than €733 million (US$823 million) were underway for new student residences and facilities upgrades.

Greece has recovered from a 2009-2018 debt crisis, when wages and education spending were cut under austerity in exchange for three international bailouts worth about €290 billion. Salaries have increased since, but real purchasing power for many Greeks is still among the lowest in the EU and has taken a fresh blow from rising inflation and soaring fuel prices linked to the Iran war.
The average monthly salary of €1,500 (US$1,685) remains stuck at the 2009 level, and many young Greeks have been priced out of housing in cities by skyrocketing rents.

"Surviving here is very difficult, the rent is really high, and the houses are really small. Our parents can’t make ends meet to pay for our rent, the electricity, for our life here," said university student Georgia Foukidou, 21, who joined the protest in Athens.
The demonstrations follow days of protests in France and Albania, where anger over rising living costs and perceived corruption has led to clashes and heavy property damage.

Protests in Greece have been largely peaceful in recent months. Mitsotakis' government has said state subsidies and other aid to prop up households and businesses against rising energy costs would reach about €1 billion.
fb9b192333f438c2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Authorities should examine how much ship emissions contribute to air pollution around major ports, particularly during haze episodes originating from Indonesia, says maritime industry expert Datuk Seri Jeyenderan M. Ramasamy.

Jeyenderan, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, said Malaysia’s strategic location along the Strait of Malacca, one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, offered significant opportunities to develop its marine fuel supply sector, but environmental considerations should not be overlooked.

“As more vessels pass through our waters, we should ensure that ship emissions are properly monitored and that our ports develop sustainably. The environmental impact of shipping activity deserves closer attention, particularly when transboundary haze affects Malaysia,” he said in a statement.
He said Port Klang and ports in Johor were strategically positioned along international shipping routes, giving Malaysia the opportunity to attract more vessels to bunker locally.

However, ships burning heavy fuel oil, including high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO), can release air pollutants such as sulphur oxides, particulate matter and other combustion-related pollutants, depending on the fuel used and engine operating conditions.
The International Maritime Organization (IMO) introduced a global sulphur limit of 0.50 per cent by mass for fuel used by ships outside designated emission control areas from January 1, 2020.

Ships may use higher-sulphur fuel if they operate under the applicable rules with an approved exhaust gas cleaning system, commonly called a scrubber. The limit for fuel used on board is separate from the rules governing HSFO carried as cargo.

Jeyenderan said the relevant authorities could consider monitoring air quality around major ports, checking compliance with marine fuel sulphur limits and studying pollution levels during haze episodes to better understand the contribution of different sources.

He stressed that reliable monitoring data would help policymakers distinguish between pollution from transboundary haze and emissions from local sources, including shipping, while supporting efforts to balance the maritime industry’s growth with environmental protection.

Echoing the call, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu adjunct professor Nazery Khalid urged the authorities to closely monitor ship emissions during haze episodes, saying Malaysia’s efforts to attract more vessels and expand seaborne trade should not come at the expense of meeting its emissions targets and its international commitments to combat climate change.

“As a responsible maritime nation and a long-standing member of the International Maritime Organization Council, Malaysia is duty-bound to ensure maritime operations in its waters are carried out in an eco-friendly manner, in full adherence to national laws and international standards.

“By ensuring emissions from shipping activities are closely monitored, even during the haze, Malaysia can also underscore its commitment to meeting its net-zero target by 2050. Shipping, which facilitates close to 90 per cent of its trade, and the maritime industry in general can play a leading role in realising this national agenda by operating sustainably,” said Nazery in the joint statement.
He also urged maritime industry stakeholders to take great care to protect the health and well-being of workers, while ensuring activities are not too severely disrupted amid the worsening haze.

“Workers involved in outdoor activities such as shipping, port operations at berthing areas and dockyards, shipbuilding or ship repair, and offshore operations should ensure their health is not compromised while carrying out their tasks,” he said.
